scope: Official FX-Clover blog text for Issue #20 P0 posts 8268, 7691, 6979, 7022, 7891 and 8090. Embedded video details are not inferred beyond official titles/descriptions when no transcript is available.

sources.title: FX ずらした移動平均線DMA【ポコニカル活用エントリーと決済について】
claims: The official page explicitly presents shifted DMA as a tool used for both entry and exit decisions and asks readers to compare the MA before and after shifting.
The page and official video description establish DMA as part of Poconical chart interpretation, but the blog text does not expose a universal machine-ready entry or exit threshold.
sources.automation_impact: Supports DMA as genuine entry/exit context. Do not invent an exact DMA cross, candle-close, distance or inside/outside threshold beyond separately reviewed primary evidence.
still_unresolved: Any universal numeric threshold not stated in primary text

sources.title: FX MAは偉大上位が下位を支配する【ポコニカル勉強会㉜】
claims: The author explicitly treats upper-timeframe MA context as dominant over lower-timeframe interpretation and says MA should be used when building the scenario.
The post says MAs can overlap at meaningful locations and explicitly includes 200MA/600MA use on upper timeframes.
In the documented H1 example, 200MA and 600MA are treated as range-like upper/lower bounds, and the same fractal idea is described as usable across timeframes.
sources.automation_impact: Strengthens upper-timeframe MA context and multi-timeframe interpretation. No universal MA-distance, slope or dominance threshold is stated.
still_unresolved: Exact quantitative definition of upper-timeframe dominance

sources.title: ライン抜けても時間足を変えれば効いてるよ【ポコニカル】
claims: The example explicitly separates H1 environment recognition from M5 execution.
A level that appears compromised on one timeframe can remain valid on another; the post gives an M15 example where the candle body did not exceed the referenced retracement level.
The Fibonacci numbers shown are example evidence, not stated as a universal entry rule for every setup.
sources.automation_impact: Supports timeframe-specific line/level interpretation. Example Fibonacci numbers must not be promoted into universal machine thresholds.
still_unresolved: Algorithm for choosing which timeframe preserves a level

sources.title: トレンドライン3-3クロスでポコニカル
claims: The documented setup keeps the upper environment fixed and uses M5 as the execution timeframe in the example.
The example stacks trendline third points, retracement context, MA compression and a three-top/right-shoulder formation before the short entry.
The author adjusts the exit when an MA obstacle appears before the farther Fibonacci target and checks whether enough room exists between entry and the next obstacle.
The author says this specific pattern is preferable on a larger timeframe and discourages the shown H1 range context.
sources.automation_impact: Supports right-shoulder/evidence stacking, room-to-obstacle checks and MA-aware exit context. It does not define a minimum room distance or a universal 3-3 cross formula.
still_unresolved: Exact minimum room to the next obstacle

sources.title: FX高勝率な200600MAパターン！チェックポイント追加【ポコニカル勉強会㊼】
claims: The post explicitly links upper-environment understanding to lower-environment entry-point narrowing.
The 200MA/600MA pattern is presented as one judgment criterion, with MA ordering, stable market conditions, thrust timing and pattern maturation highlighted.
The author presents point-scoring of confluences only as an optional idea using placeholder scores, not a fixed official numeric scoring system.
sources.automation_impact: Supports contextual 200/600 pattern evaluation and confluence ranking. Do not create numeric scores or a fixed entry threshold from placeholder examples.

sources.title: FX 1時間のMAとレートの位置関係でロジックを選ぶ【ポコニカル勉強会58】
claims: The author explicitly says the relationship between MA and price determines which logic/setup is used.
If the expected 200MA/600MA pattern does not form, the post explicitly allows passing on that pattern and considering another known setup instead.
H1 MA/neck context is used to constrain exits and no-trade decisions, while MA above price with no obstacle is treated as favorable in the shown short setup.
The post uses 3-3 as an exit discriminator in an example, while existing master-course evidence states that 3-3 is not universally mandatory.
sources.automation_impact: Supports context-dependent setup selection and MA-path/obstacle awareness. It does not justify making 200/600 or 3-3 universally mandatory or adding a numeric obstacle threshold.
still_unresolved: Exact 3-3 exit formula outside the example

production_policy: No v1.23 WATCH/READY/TRIGGER behavior change and no new numeric READY/TRIGGER threshold are justified by this batch. Preserve orders_enabled:false and keep unresolved fine-grained rules in research/manual interpretation.
